props.name: align
props.description: How to align the popup relative to the specified side.

props.name: anchor
props.type: Element | null | VirtualElement | React.RefObject<Element | null> | (() => Element | VirtualElement | null) | undefined
props.description:
An element to position the popup against.
By default, the popup will be positioned against the trigger.

props.name: positionMethod
props.description: Determines which CSS `position` property to use.

props.name: side
props.description:
Which side of the anchor element to align the popup against.
May automatically change to avoid collisions.

props.name: sideOffset
props.description:
Distance between the anchor and the popup in pixels.
Also accepts a function that returns the distance to read the dimensions of the anchor
and positioner elements, along with its side and alignment.

The function takes a `data` object parameter with the following properties:
- `data.anchor`: the dimensions of the anchor element with properties `width` and `height`.
- `data.positioner`: the dimensions of the positioner element with properties `width` and `height`.
- `data.side`: which side of the anchor element the positioner is aligned against.
- `data.align`: how the positioner is aligned relative to the specified side.

props.name: alignOffset
props.description:
Additional offset along the alignment axis in pixels.
Also accepts a function that returns the offset to read the dimensions of the anchor
and positioner elements, along with its side and alignment.

The function takes a `data` object parameter with the following properties:
- `data.anchor`: the dimensions of the anchor element with properties `width` and `height`.
- `data.positioner`: the dimensions of the positioner element with properties `width` and `height`.
- `data.side`: which side of the anchor element the positioner is aligned against.
- `data.align`: how the positioner is aligned relative to the specified side.

props.name: collisionBoundary
props.description: An element or a rectangle that delimits the area that the popup is confined to.

props.name: collisionPadding
props.description: Additional space to maintain from the edge of the collision boundary.

props.name: sticky
props.description:
Whether to maintain the popup in the viewport after
the anchor element was scrolled out of view.

props.name: arrowPadding
props.description:
Minimum distance to maintain between the arrow and the edges of the popup.

Use it to prevent the arrow element from hanging out of the rounded corners of a popup.

props.name: disableAnchorTracking
props.description: Whether to disable the popup from tracking any layout shift of its positioning anchor.

props.name: collisionAvoidance
props.description:
Determines how to handle collisions when positioning the popup.

`side` controls overflow on the preferred placement axis (`top`/`bottom` or `left`/`right`):
- `'flip'`: keep the requested side when it fits; otherwise try the opposite side
  (`top` and `bottom`, or `left` and `right`).
- `'shift'`: never change side; keep the requested side and move the popup within
  the clipping boundary so it stays visible.
- `'none'`: do not correct side-axis overflow.

`align` controls overflow on the alignment axis (`start`/`center`/`end`):
- `'flip'`: keep side, but swap `start` and `end` when the requested alignment overflows.
- `'shift'`: keep side and requested alignment, then nudge the popup along the
  alignment axis to fit.
- `'none'`: do not correct alignment-axis overflow.

`fallbackAxisSide` controls fallback behavior on the perpendicular axis when the
preferred axis cannot fit:
- `'start'`: allow perpendicular fallback and try the logical start side first
  (`top` before `bottom`, or `left` before `right` in LTR).
- `'end'`: allow perpendicular fallback and try the logical end side first
  (`bottom` before `top`, or `right` before `left` in LTR).
- `'none'`: do not fallback to the perpendicular axis.

When `side` is `'shift'`, explicitly setting `align` only supports `'shift'` or `'none'`.
If `align` is omitted, it defaults to `'flip'`.

props.name: initialFocus
props.type: boolean | React.RefObject<HTMLElement | null> | ((openType: InteractionType) => void | boolean | HTMLElement | null) | undefined
props.description:
Determines the element to focus when the popup is opened.

- `false`: Do not move focus.
- `true`: Move focus based on the default behavior (first tabbable element or popup).
- `RefObject`: Move focus to the ref element.
- `function`: Called with the interaction type (`mouse`, `touch`, `pen`, or `keyboard`).
  Return an element to focus, `true` to use the default behavior, or `false`/`undefined` to do nothing.

props.name: finalFocus
props.type: boolean | React.RefObject<HTMLElement | null> | ((closeType: InteractionType) => void | boolean | HTMLElement | null) | undefined
props.description:
Determines the element to focus when the popup is closed.

- `false`: Do not move focus.
- `true`: Move focus based on the default behavior (trigger or previously focused element).
- `RefObject`: Move focus to the ref element.
- `function`: Called with the interaction type (`mouse`, `touch`, `pen`, or `keyboard`).
  Return an element to focus, `true` to use the default behavior, or `false`/`undefined` to do nothing.

props.name: container
props.type: HTMLElement | ShadowRoot | React.RefObject<HTMLElement | ShadowRoot | null> | null | undefined
props.description: A parent element to render the portal element into.

props.name: form
props.description:
Identifies the form that owns the internal input.
Useful when the combobox is rendered outside the form.

props.name: filter
props.type: null | ((item: Item, query: string, itemToString?: (item: Item) => string) => boolean) | undefined
props.description:
Filter function used to match items vs input query.
Receives the source item, which is the derived value's item when `items` is a `createItems()`
collection, and the item itself otherwise.

props.name: id
props.description: The id of the component.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Whether the component should ignore user interaction.

props.name: loopFocus
props.description:
Whether to loop keyboard focus back to the input when the end of the list is reached while using the arrow keys. The first item can then be reached by pressing <kbd>ArrowDown</kbd> again from the input, or the last item can be reached by pressing <kbd>ArrowUp</kbd> from the input.
The input is always included in the focus loop per [ARIA Authoring Practices](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/combobox/).
When disabled, focus does not move when on the last element and the user presses <kbd>ArrowDown</kbd>, or when on the first element and the user presses <kbd>ArrowUp</kbd>.

props.name: name
props.description: Identifies the field when a form is submitted.

props.name: readOnly
props.description: Whether the user should be unable to choose a different option from the popup.

props.name: required
props.description: Whether the user must choose a value before submitting a form.

props.name: inputRef
props.description: A ref to the hidden input element.

props.name: open
props.description: Whether the popup is currently open. Use when controlled.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description:
Whether the popup is initially open.

To render a controlled popup, use the `open` prop instead.

props.name: onOpenChangeComplete
props.description: Event handler called after any animations complete when the popup is opened or closed.

props.name: openOnInputClick
props.description: Whether the popup opens when clicking the input.

props.name: inputValue
props.description: The input value of the combobox. Use when controlled.

props.name: defaultInputValue
props.description:
The uncontrolled input value when initially rendered.

To render a controlled input, use the `inputValue` prop instead.

props.name: grid
props.description:
Whether list items are presented in a grid layout.
When enabled, arrow keys navigate across rows and columns inferred from DOM rows.

props.name: items
props.type: readonly any[] | readonly Group<any>[] | ComboboxItemCollection<Item, ItemValue> | undefined
props.description:
The items to be displayed in the list.
Can be a flat array of items, an array of groups with items, or a collection created by
the `createItems()` function, which derives each item's selection value and label.
Nullish entries are not supported: remove them from the data before passing it.

props.name: filteredItems
props.description:
Filtered items to display in the list.
When provided, the list uses these items instead of filtering the `items` prop internally.
When `items` is also provided, this array must preserve its flat or grouped structure.
With a `createItems()` collection, pass source items rather than derived values.
Nullish entries are not supported, as in `items`.
Use when you want to control filtering logic externally with the `useFilter()` hook.

props.name: virtualized
props.description: Whether the items are being externally virtualized.

props.name: inline
props.description:
Whether the list is rendered inline without using the component's own popup.

Specify `open` unconditionally in conjunction with this prop so the list is considered
visible: `<Combobox.Root inline open>`

In a `Combobox.Root` > `Dialog.Root` composition, bind the Combobox's `open` and
`onOpenChange` props to the `Dialog`'s `open` and `onOpenChange` state instead so the
component resets its transient state (filter query, highlighted item, and input value) when
the dialog closes.

props.name: modal
props.description:
Determines if the popup enters a modal state when open.
- `true`: user interaction is limited to the popup: document page scroll is locked and pointer interactions on outside elements are disabled.
- `false`: user interaction with the rest of the document is allowed.

On touch devices, a `true` modal blocks outside taps but leaves the page scrollable unless the popup spans nearly the full viewport width, matching native iOS behavior.

props.name: limit
props.description: The maximum number of items to display in the list.

props.name: locale
props.description:
The locale to use for string comparison.
Defaults to the user's runtime locale.

props.name: multiple
props.description: Whether multiple items can be selected.

props.name: autoComplete
props.description: Provides a hint to the browser for autofill.

props.name: autoHighlight
props.description: Whether the first matching item is highlighted automatically while filtering.

props.name: highlightItemOnHover
props.description:
Whether moving the pointer over items should highlight them.
Disabling this prop allows CSS `:hover` to be differentiated from the `:focus` (`data-highlighted`) state.

props.name: itemToStringLabel
props.description:
When the item values are objects (`<Combobox.Item value={object}>`), this function converts the object value to a string representation for display in the input.
If the shape of the object is `{ value, label }`, the label will be used automatically without needing to specify this prop.
With a `createItems()` collection, this receives the derived value, and the collection's
`getLabel` takes precedence for values it can resolve.

props.name: itemToStringValue
props.description:
When the item values are objects (`<Combobox.Item value={object}>`), this function converts the object value to a string representation for form submission.
If the shape of the object is `{ value, label }`, the value will be used automatically without needing to specify this prop.
With a `createItems()` collection, this receives the derived value.

props.name: isItemEqualToValue
props.description:
Custom comparison logic used to determine if a combobox item value matches the current selected value. Useful when item values are objects without matching referentially.
With a `createItems()` collection, both arguments are derived values.
Defaults to `Object.is` comparison.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description:
The uncontrolled selected value of the combobox when it's initially rendered.

To render a controlled combobox, use the `value` prop instead.

props.name: actionsRef
props.description:
A ref to imperative actions.
- `unmount`: Ends the closing phase of the combobox after an externally controlled closing animation finishes.
Call `preventUnmountOnClose()` in `onOpenChange` first, otherwise the combobox completes closing on its own.
Whether it leaves the DOM is decided by `keepMounted` on the portal.
- `close`: Closes the combobox imperatively when called.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Event handler called when the popup is opened or closed.

props.name: onInputValueChange
props.description: Event handler called when the input value changes.

props.name: onItemHighlighted
props.type: ((highlightedValue: Value | undefined, eventDetails: ComboboxRoot.HighlightEventDetails) => void) | undefined
props.description:
Callback fired when an item is highlighted or unhighlighted.
Receives the highlighted item value (or `undefined` if no item is highlighted) and event details with a `reason` property describing why the highlight changed.
The `reason` can be:
- `'keyboard'`: the highlight changed due to keyboard navigation.
- `'pointer'`: the highlight changed due to pointer hovering. The event may be a `MouseEvent`
  rather than a `PointerEvent`.
- `'none'`: the highlight changed for another reason, such as typing, `autoHighlight`, the
  item list changing, or the popup opening or closing.

props.name: value
props.description: The selected value of the combobox. Use when controlled.

props.name: onValueChange
props.type: ((value: ComboboxOutputValue<Value, Multiple> | (Multiple extends true ? never : null), eventDetails: ComboboxRoot.ChangeEventDetails) => void) | undefined
props.description: Event handler called when the selected value of the combobox changes.

props.name: children
props.description:
Accepts a function that returns a `ReactNode` to format the selected value.
Treat the value as read-only: in `multiple` mode it may be a shared frozen array
when nothing is selected.

props.name: placeholder
props.description:
The placeholder value to display when no value is selected.
This is overridden by `children` if specified, or by a null item's label in `items`.
